strategy.index_policy: Only curated high-intent comparisons are indexable. Arbitrary model selections are available in the interactive compare builder without generating thin crawlable URLs.
strategy.evidence_policy: Generated comparison facts must come from data/model-pricing.json and data/model-history.json. No benchmark, speed, quality, or winner claim may be inferred from specifications alone.
strategy.pricing_policy: Direct token-cost comparisons are shown only when both models have calculator-eligible provider-published Standard paid pricing.

comparisons.title: Nano Banana 2.1 vs Nano Banana Pro
comparisons.summary: Compare Google's efficient Nano Banana 2.1 and premium Nano Banana Pro on image pricing, output resolutions, model identifiers, context and creative workflows using primary sources.

specialist_factors.title: 1K and 2K image output
specialist_factors.detail: Google estimates Nano Banana 2.1 at $0.0336 per 1K image or $0.0504 per 2K image, versus Nano Banana Pro at $0.134 for a 1K or 2K image. Those output-only estimates exclude input and grounding costs.

specialist_factors.title: 4K image output
specialist_factors.detail: Google estimates $0.113 per generated 4K image for Nano Banana 2.1 versus $0.24 for Nano Banana Pro. Image tokens and separately billed text/thinking tokens should not be conflated.

specialist_factors.title: Choose by creative workflow
specialist_factors.detail: Nano Banana 2.1 targets efficient conversational editing, high throughput and consistent multi-reference subjects. Nano Banana Pro targets advanced graphic design, precision creative control and complex high-fidelity compositions.

specialist_factors.title: No invented quality benchmark
specialist_factors.detail: Neither model has an SXF verified side-by-side image quality score here. Test actual brand copy, compositing, edit consistency and typography on your own prompts.

comparisons.title: Kling VIDEO 3.0 vs Seedance 2.0
comparisons.summary: Compare Kling VIDEO 3.0 and ByteDance Seedance 2.0 on native-audio video generation, reference inputs, duration, official access and their incompatible native pricing units.

specialist_factors.title: Inputs and direction
specialist_factors.detail: Kling 3.0 officially supports text-to-video, image-to-video, reference elements and multi-shot prompts. Seedance 2.0 supports text, images, video clips and audio clips as multimodal references.

specialist_factors.title: Clip length and sound
specialist_factors.detail: Both platforms document up to 15-second video generation with native audio capabilities. Duration, aspect ratio, credits and resulting quality depend on mode and deployment.

specialist_factors.title: Pricing is not directly interchangeable
specialist_factors.detail: Kling's product guide publishes Credits per generated second (e.g. 6 Credits/s for 720p without audio), while BytePlus publishes Seedance 2.0 USD per million metered service tokens, varying with resolution and video inputs. No universal USD-per-video winner can be calculated.

specialist_factors.title: Official API availability
specialist_factors.detail: Kling exposes a developer text-to-video/kling-3.0 endpoint. Seedance 2.0 is available as dreamina-seedance-2-0-260128 on BytePlus ModelArk, subject to deployment and account availability.

comparisons.title: GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst vs Flare
comparisons.summary: Compare Sunburst and Flare on supported image workflow, published modality-specific token prices, editing capability and performance claims without assuming equal output token consumption.

specialist_factors.title: Published Image API token rates
specialist_factors.detail: Both models publish $8 image input, $2 cached image input and $30 image output per million image tokens in Standard pricing. Prompt text charges are separate ($5 input and $1.25 cached per 1M text tokens).

specialist_factors.title: Different positioning
specialist_factors.detail: OpenAI describes Flare as its fastest model for high-quality everyday images. Sunburst targets high-fidelity image generation and precise editing. No independent SXF speed or quality benchmark is claimed.

specialist_factors.title: Compare actual image cost
specialist_factors.detail: Equal token rates do not imply identical cost per picture: generated image-token consumption varies with chosen output size, quality and model implementation.

specialist_factors.title: Practical choice
specialist_factors.detail: Try Flare for speed-sensitive interactive iteration, and Sunburst for complex high-precision image editing; evaluate samples on the same prompt.

comparisons.title: Eleven v4 vs Eleven v4 Turbo
comparisons.summary: Compare ElevenLabs flagship expressive text-to-speech variants on use cases, supported languages, latency claims, streaming and credit-based billing.

specialist_factors.title: Delivery priority
specialist_factors.detail: Eleven v4 targets expressive narration, audiobooks, long-form dialogue and voice cloning. Eleven v4 Turbo targets responsive interactive applications and agents.

specialist_factors.title: Provider latency claim
specialist_factors.detail: ElevenLabs quotes about 100 ms median inference latency for v4 Turbo. This is a vendor-published figure, not an independently measured end-to-end latency.

specialist_factors.title: Billing clarity
specialist_factors.detail: ElevenLabs describes a character/credit-based TTS service with subscription-specific pricing. No universal verified USD/1K-character API figure is asserted for these new variants.

specialist_factors.title: Language coverage
specialist_factors.detail: The Eleven v4 family supports 90+ languages including Arabic. Check voice availability, tags and agent integration for your exact task.

comparisons.title: Gemini Omni Flash vs Kling VIDEO 3.0
comparisons.summary: Compare Google conversational video editing and Kling narrative video generation on input modes, video duration and incompatible per-token versus credit pricing.

specialist_factors.title: Conversational editing
specialist_factors.detail: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash supports iterative video editing and extensions via Google Interactions API; Kling VIDEO 3.0 emphasizes creative text/image-to-video, multi-shot sequencing and optional audio.

specialist_factors.title: Published duration
specialist_factors.detail: Gemini Omni Flash supports 3–10 seconds of video output, while Kling 3.0 product documentation references 3–15 seconds for supported modes. Actual constraints depend on configuration.

specialist_factors.title: Do not compare unlike rates
specialist_factors.detail: Gemini Omni quotes $17.50 per 1M video output tokens (about $0.10/sec at 720p) and separate input costs; Kling publishes consumer-plan Credits/second but not a verified equivalent USD API rate.

specialist_factors.title: Best evaluation
specialist_factors.detail: Compare storyboard consistency, editability, motion, sound and total clip cost on identical workflow settings.

comparisons.title: FLUX.2 Max vs Nano Banana Pro
comparisons.summary: Compare premium image generation and image editing for brand consistency, output pricing units, text rendering and production workflows.

specialist_factors.title: Different cost units
specialist_factors.detail: FLUX.2 Max starts at $0.07 for the first output MP, adds $0.03 per additional MP and $0.03 per reference-input MP. Nano Banana Pro lists $0.134 per 1K/2K image and $0.24 per 4K image (output-only estimates).

specialist_factors.title: Workflow fit
specialist_factors.detail: FLUX.2 Max focuses on product visualization, reference consistency, layout and grounded visual generation. Nano Banana Pro focuses on precise typography, product mockups and complex image edits.

specialist_factors.title: Hidden input charges
specialist_factors.detail: Image references and output resolutions affect FLUX charges; Nano Banana input text, image tokens and grounding can add charges. A universal per-image winner is not supported.

specialist_factors.title: No invented quality score
specialist_factors.detail: These are official product capabilities, not an SXF image benchmark. Reproduce tasks with the same style, resolution and source assets to decide.

comparisons.title: GPT-Image-2 vs GPT-Image-2.5 Flare
comparisons.summary: Compare GPT-Image-2 vs GPT-Image-2.5 Flare using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: Official IMAGE-token pricing
specialist_factors.detail: GPT-Image-2 Standard image tokens are $4 input, $1 cached and $15 output per million. Flare costs $8 input, $2 cached and $30 output. Both separately charge prompt TEXT tokens; equal images may consume different tokens.

specialist_factors.title: Choose by production needs
specialist_factors.detail: GPT-Image-2 emphasizes accessible image generation and editing. Flare emphasizes fast high-quality image output within the 2.5 line.

specialist_factors.title: Measure effective per-image cost
specialist_factors.detail: Image resolution, number of references, input text and quality settings change the final bill; multiplying token rates alone is insufficient.

comparisons.title: Ideogram 4.0 vs Ideogram 3.0
comparisons.summary: Compare Ideogram 4.0 vs Ideogram 3.0 using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: Official TURBO prices
specialist_factors.detail: Both providers list $0.03 for a single TURBO output image. Ideogram 4.0 DEFAULT is $0.06 and QUALITY $0.10; Ideogram 3.0 DEFAULT is $0.06 and QUALITY $0.09.

specialist_factors.title: Creative controls
specialist_factors.detail: Ideogram 4.0 supports structured prompting and newer layouts for text-centric design; Ideogram 3.0 has a stable established Remix, Edit and Reframe API contract.

specialist_factors.title: No synthetic quality winner
specialist_factors.detail: Run identical logo, poster, typography and editing prompts across matched speed and size settings before deciding.

comparisons.title: Runway Gen-4.5 vs Kling VIDEO 3.0
comparisons.summary: Compare Runway Gen-4.5 vs Kling VIDEO 3.0 using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: Comparable output duration
specialist_factors.detail: Runway Gen-4.5 is documented for 2–10-second text/image-to-video clips and its API uses 12 developer credits/second. Kling 3.0 creator docs describe 3–15-second clips and varying credits by mode.

specialist_factors.title: Native billing
specialist_factors.detail: Runway API sells credits at $0.01, resulting in $0.12/second for standard Gen-4.5 video, excluding HDR surcharges. Kling credits are consumer-plan references and must not be falsely converted into a universal USD API figure.

specialist_factors.title: Production tradeoffs
specialist_factors.detail: Test camera movement, temporal consistency, prompt adherence, audio modes and output resolution on your real storyboard.

comparisons.title: Deepgram Nova-3 vs ElevenLabs Scribe v2
comparisons.summary: Compare Deepgram Nova-3 vs ElevenLabs Scribe v2 using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: Audio-time pricing
specialist_factors.detail: Deepgram Nova-3 lists pre-recorded MONOLINGUAL $0.0043/min ($0.258/hour). ElevenLabs Scribe v2 lists $0.22/hour. Different add-on policies and multilingual modes affect effective cost.

specialist_factors.title: Language and diarization
specialist_factors.detail: Compare language support, accuracy on calls and accents, word-level timing, speaker diarization and keyterm prompting for each workflow.

specialist_factors.title: Different modes
specialist_factors.detail: Nova-3 supports prerecorded and streaming with separate rate cards; Scribe v2 is focused on file/batch STT, and ElevenLabs has Scribe Realtime for streaming.

comparisons.title: Deepgram Flux vs Scribe v2 Realtime
comparisons.summary: Compare Deepgram Flux vs Scribe v2 Realtime using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: Published native prices
specialist_factors.detail: Deepgram Flux English uses a time-limited $0.0065/min streaming rate; Scribe v2 Realtime lists $0.39/hour (also $0.0065/min). Provider promotions and voice-activity policies may change real costs.

specialist_factors.title: Turn detection
specialist_factors.detail: Flux offers speech recognition plus integrated end-of-turn detection. Scribe Realtime offers partial/final transcripts and VAD-assisted commits via WebSocket.

specialist_factors.title: Latency decisions
specialist_factors.detail: Compare end-of-turn latency, interruption accuracy, reliability and accented/multilingual speech using your own agent sessions.

comparisons.title: FLUX.2 Pro vs Klein 9B
comparisons.summary: Compare FLUX.2 Pro vs Klein 9B using official sources, cost units, supported workflows and provider access, with no fabricated benchmark winner.

specialist_factors.title: BFL first-MP prices
specialist_factors.detail: FLUX.2 Pro starts at $0.03 per first output MP; Klein 9B at $0.015. Additional output and reference-image megapixels have separate model-specific rates.

specialist_factors.title: Hosting options
specialist_factors.detail: FLUX.2 Klein 9B is available as licensed open weights and an API. FLUX.2 Pro is offered as a hosted BFL API model.

specialist_factors.title: Workload-specific choice
specialist_factors.detail: Evaluate design fidelity, speed and edit consistency at identical resolutions. Prices here refer to first output MP, not fixed costs for all image sizes.
